mainEntity.name: What is the #1 best wood fence style for Oakland County homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: For most Oakland County homeowners, board-on-board in pressure-treated pine delivers the best overall value balancing privacy, durability, aesthetics, and cost. Cedar board-on-board is the premium recommendation for the highest-end look.

mainEntity.name: Cedar vs. pressure-treated pine — which is better for Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cedar is the premium choice — naturally rot and insect resistant with beautiful aging. Pressure-treated pine is the practical budget choice, chemically protected and significantly cheaper. Avoid untreated spruce, fir, or white pine for Michigan fences.

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit for a wood fence in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in most Oakland County cities and townships including Auburn Hills, Rochester Hills, Troy, and Birmingham. BF Fence handles the permit process for you on every project.

mainEntity.name: What fence styles are HOA-friendly in Oakland County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Oakland County HOAs allow board-on-board, shadowbox, and dog-ear picket styles. Horizontal slat and split-rail may require pre-approval. Always check your HOA's architectural guidelines before finalizing plans.

mainEntity.name: How often should I stain or seal my wood fence in Michigan?

acceptedAnswer.text: Pressure-treated pine needs staining/sealing every 3-4 years. Cedar every 2-3 years. Regular maintenance nearly doubles the lifespan of a wood fence in Michigan's climate.

mainEntity.name: Can I mix fence styles on the same property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A common approach is dog-ear picket in the front yard for curb appeal and board-on-board privacy in the backyard. The transition between styles at the corner of the house just needs a clean post and consistent material.
